newsitem.title: UK: UK's Sunday shoppers favour food superstores.
newsitem.headline: UK's Sunday shoppers favour food superstores.

text.p: Two years on from the introduction of Sunday shopping in Britain, supermarkets seem to be faring best from the relaxation of trading rules.

According to a survey by real estate consultants Healy and Baker, 76 percent of consumers buy food and groceries on Sunday, 26 percent spend money in do-it-yourself stores and 22 percent in garden centres.

Fewer than 10 percent of Sunday shoppers visit town centres and shopping centres, and the sort of shops these centres offer on Sunday still appear to be less popular than those found out of town, it said.

Consumers said they wanted more department stores to open on Sundays as well as Marks and Spencer Plc and Boots Co Plc. "These are the two names that most frequently mentioned by consumers when asked which of the stores -- not normally open on a Sunday -- they would like to shop in," the survey said.
Others included John Lewis, Woolworths, Debenhams, BhS and Argos.
Healey and Baker's survey was compiled from a combination of 20 retail locations, a telephone survey of individual consumers and 25 leading retailers.
